allometry.note: 0.03 m: the low end of the stated 3-10 cm, as Flora of North America's stems are more often procumbent, rooting at the nodes, so the mat stands about as tall as its ascending tips and pedicels. Not measured.

traits.seed_dispersal.note: Wikipedia, Sagina procumbens (read 2026-11-02): it reached Gough Island as seed on visitors' boots or clothes, so feet carry it.

traits.trampling_tolerance.note: Flora of North America, Sagina procumbens: grows on gravel and sand by roads, in pavement cracks and at the edges of paths and lawns.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America (Sagina procumbens): perennial, often mat-forming, glabrous. Stems ascending or, more frequently, procumbent, rooting at nodes, giving rise to secondary tufts or rosettes, few- to many-branched, slender. Basal leaves frequently in primary rosettes, blade linear, 8-17 mm, apex apiculate to somewhat aristate; cauline blade linear, 4-15 mm proximally, 2.5-6 mm distally. Flowers axillary or terminal, 4-merous; petals 0.8-1 mm, shorter than or equaling sepals 1.5-2.5 mm. Flora of China: stems 3-10 cm tall; leaves 2-10 x 1-2 mm.
